references.text: The context of Moses' action: he saw an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, which led him to kill the Egyptian in verse 12.
A Hebrew confronts Moses and asks if he intends to kill him as he killed the Egyptian, showing that the murder had become known.
Pharaoh heard about the killing and sought to put Moses to death, causing Moses to flee to Midian.
Stephen refers to this event in his speech: καὶ ἰδών τινα ἀδικούμενον ἠμύνατο καὶ ἐποίησεν ἐκδίκησιν τῷ καταπονουμένῳ πατάξας τὸν Αἰγύπτιον - Moses struck the Egyptian and avenged the oppressed.
Stephen explains that Moses believed his brothers would understand that God intended to save them through him.
Reference to the killing in Stephen's speech: μὴ ἀνελεῖν με σὺ θέλεις ὃν τρόπον ἀνεῖλες ἐχθὲς τὸν Αἰγύπτιον - 'Do you intend to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?'
By faith Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter and chose to suffer with God's people - context for why he acted in defense of the Hebrews.
